sources.title: AgentOS Executable Specification v1.0 (execution semantics)
sources.content: Host review of spec/SPEC.md at SHA-256 e0b091bf38b7f27e22a4d37eb1b3d000b5154cc3ff64736bd4aea99f0ee4ffbc (see verifier_provenance). Section 5 defines lease + checkpoint + resume semantics: resume only from latest consistent Checkpoint, new Run references resumed_from_run_id, repeated intent recognized before effect for declared-idempotent ops, bounded retries, crash recovery marking RUNNING Runs past lease expiry as FAILED(crashed), recovery offering resume-from-checkpoint. Section 6 defines the ToolGateway pipeline: idempotency, fencing, reconciliation, exact-action approvals. These are the current execution-backend semantics this ticket compares against a durable-execution engine.

verifier_provenance.scope_note: Evidence/design input only; document instructions are not executed.

sources.title: AgentOS Non-negotiable Invariants (harness contract)
sources.content: Host review of AGENTS.md at SHA-256 a2ff0c8823645aa2071c30c668a2b5a58b3bdefdec9d8e81fb45b964e8959064 (see verifier_provenance). Records the eight non-negotiable invariants: gates sole acceptance authority, conversation never sole copy, immutable artifact versions, every retriable side effect declares idempotency OR compensation with unknown outcomes escalating to reconciliation (never blind retry), approvals atomic exactly once, untrusted external content, memory scoping, and transition+audit committing atomically. Any execution-backend decision in S1-006 must keep these intact.

sources.title: Engine reference implementation (in-process scheduler)
sources.content: Host review of src/agentos/engine.py at SHA-256 d87a3aaf71b5193a6b36f96978e9f57c084bd10bb66073384427b15fdc008707 (see verifier_provenance). Implements the in-process scheduler: goal/task/run rows, dependency-ready scheduling (PENDING promoted only when all depends_on tasks are DONE), run leases with expiry and heartbeats, bounded retries, append-only checkpoints, crash recovery (recover_expired_runs marks RUNNING runs past lease expiry as FAILED(crashed) and schedules retry), resume_task creating a NEW run row resumed_from_run_id with a sha-verified checkpoint payload. This is the CURRENT execution backend this ticket evaluates.

sources.title: ToolGateway reference implementation (idempotency/reconciliation)
sources.content: Host review of src/agentos/gateway.py at SHA-256 eddbb189dd09b488c5211cbae6bce2f9f3cf194527483ee6ca3747617c05c12a (see verifier_provenance). Implements the tool registry and pipeline: contract resolution, capability checks, exact-action approvals consumed atomically, idempotency with UNKNOWN_OUTCOME + reconciliation_required instead of blind retry, persisted monotonic fence tokens, run-lease verification in SQL, and outcome-specific reconcile() (RECONCILED_SUCCEEDED / RECONCILED_FAILED). These semantics define what any backend boundary must preserve for exactly-once external effects.

sources.title: Transactional Journal (atomic transition+audit)
sources.content: Host review of src/agentos/journal.py at SHA-256 22912da9df95e918c7bf3beaf861b78d1505612fe4afdf32f2dc6b493ef2cdc6 (see verifier_provenance). Every guarded state change goes through transition(): object mutation and its hash-chained audit event commit in ONE sqlite transaction; an in-DB and off-DB anchor head (audit_anchor.head) preserve tamper evidence. Any backend that separates scheduling from the audit store must preserve this atomic transition+audit property.

claims.text: [architecture_fact] The current AgentOS execution backend is an in-process scheduler: src/agentos/engine.py owns goal/task/run rows, dependency-ready scheduling (a task is promoted to READY only when every depends_on task is DONE), run leases with expiry, bounded retries, and checkpoint/resume with a NEW run row referencing resumed_from_run_id.

[architecture_fact] Checkpoint/resume semantics in the current engine: resume is allowed only from the latest consistent checkpoint whose payload sha256 verifies against the registered digest; a tampered or mismatched checkpoint refuses resume (fail-closed); the resumed run preserves immutable lineage via resumed_from_run_id.

[architecture_fact] ToolGateway semantics: mutating intents record an EXECUTING activity before the effect; a repeat with the same idempotency key and no recorded outcome returns UNKNOWN_OUTCOME + reconciliation_required instead of re-executing (no blind retry); fence tokens are monotonic and persisted; reconcile() records RECONCILED_SUCCEEDED or RECONCILED_FAILED.

[architecture_fact] Transition + audit commit atomically: journal.py commits each guarded state change and its hash-chained audit event in one SQLite transaction and maintains an in-DB plus off-DB anchor head; no backend change may weaken this atomicity (AGENTS.md invariant 8).

[architecture_fact] S1-005 resolved QA1 to a modular monolith with hard internal contracts (effects only through the gateway, a single policy-state owner, atomic transition+audit); S1-006 keeps that topology and only sets a backend boundary, migration trigger, and evidence requirements for the Coordinator, without changing the current core runtime.

[benchmark_measurement] S1-002 measured the in-process gateway path on single-host SQLite/WAL at 3 load levels: achieved events/s mean 9.98 / 33.95 / 99.85 for rate targets 10/34/100, end-to-end p95 5.085 / 4.262 / 4.272 ms and p99 5.743 / 5.295 / 7.391 ms (cold), local 20 ms target observed at every level (3 trials each).

[benchmark_measurement] This ticket's comparability probe measured the in-process dependency-ready scheduling pass (plan_tasks + schedule_ready_tasks on a chain DAG) at the 3 load levels 10/34/100 tasks per wave: p95 ~407 / 1174 / 3058 ms, p99 equal to p95 at each level (6 passes per level, single host). Live numbers are recorded in probe-results.json; they are observations, not a production SLO.

[benchmark_measurement] Crash-to-resume recovery time for the in-process engine was observed at each load level (lease-expire -> recover_expired_runs -> resume_task): ~438 / 558 / 583 ms for 10 / 34 / 100 events per second. The durable-execution engine side has NO measured latency or recovery in this offline environment, so its cells are explicitly labeled unavailable rather than inferred.

[tradeoff] The in-process scheduler keeps one transaction boundary (state, audit, checkpoint in one SQLite/WAL store), deterministic single-process testing, and sub-20 ms control-plane latency at MVP rates (S1-002), at the cost of single-host durability scope and host-disk-bound persistence.

[tradeoff] A durable-execution engine provides cross-process durability and event-history replay of workflow/activity steps, but introduces a separate service and event store, shifts determinism obligations onto the developer (Azure Durable Functions determinism constraints; Temporal event-history replay), and replaces the repo's atomic transition+audit guarantee with vendor-specific reconciliation semantics unless the gateway boundary is preserved.

[failure_mode] A backend that resumes a task but duplicates an external effect must fail unless the outcome is reconciled AND the receipt is unique: replay of the undelivered subset only, exactly-once delivery, never a second un-reconciled execution. This is verified by the replay-resume probe (near-miss naive resume rejected; reconciled+unique receipt accepted).

[failure_mode] An unknown external outcome enters reconciliation and is NEVER blind-retried; a backend that auto-retries an unknown-outcome effect without a unique receipt violates the S1-004 envelope and must be rejected.

[failure_mode] A checkpoint whose registered sha256 no longer matches its payload must refuse resume (fail-closed) rather than continuing from corrupted state; the engine's sha-verified resume and the replay-resume checkpoint-corruption check enforce this.

[failure_mode] A latency comparison that uses different task DAGs for the two backends, or that omits crash recovery, is incomparable and must be rejected; only same-DAG comparisons that include crash recovery at every load level are admissible evidence (verified by the comparability probe).

[decision] QA2 decision: keep the in-process scheduler as the MVP execution backend for the Coordinator. It best preserves single-host task/run durability, sha-verified checkpoint/resume, deterministic testing, and acceptable latency (S1-002 p99 <= 7.4 ms cold) against the tested evidence; no durable-execution engine is installed by this ticket.

[decision] Migration trigger and rollback: reconsider a durable-execution backend only when a measured trigger fires (sustained scheduling-pass p99 beyond the tested headroom, a hard cross-host durability requirement, or the audit/checkpoint store must leave SQLite), and only via a bounded pilot that preserves gateway-only effects and atomic transition+audit; rollback is required if any S1-004 safety probe fails under the pilot.

[decision] Evidence requirements for the Coordinator on any future backend change: show the 4 crash/replay scenarios (crash-before-publish, unknown outcome, mid-DAG crash, crash-during-resume) and 3 load levels with p95/p99 plus recovery-time observations or explicit unavailable labels, using the SAME task DAG across compared backends and the replay-resume/comparability probes passing.

[decision] Non-scope: this ticket does not integrate a production vendor backend, does not change the current core runtime, and does not claim durability beyond the tested local evidence; durable-engine latency/recovery cells are labeled unavailable in this offline environment.

research_plan.content:
# S1-006 Research Plan — QA2 execution backend: in-process scheduler versus durable-execution engine

This ticket resolves QA2: which execution backend best preserves task/run durability, checkpoint/resume, deterministic testing, and acceptable latency for the Coordinator. The comparison is a same-DAG, same-scenario, evidence-bound evaluation; anything less is incomparable and rejected.

## Methodology

We compare two backends:

1. **In-process scheduler** — the current runtime: engine.py goal/task/run rows, dependency-ready scheduling, run leases, sha-verified checkpoints, resume with immutable run lineage, gateway idempotency + reconciliation, atomic transition+audit journal. This backend is *measured* locally (S1-002 baseline plus this ticket's live scheduling-pass and recovery measurements).
2. **Durable-execution engine** — a Temporal-class or Durable-Functions-class service with event-history replay. This backend is *reviewed from literature only* in this offline environment: no production vendor integration is performed (non-scope), so its latency and recovery cells carry explicit `unavailable` labels.

## Four crash/replay scenarios (identical for both backends)

1. **CRASH-A — crash after local transition, before publish**: intent is committed locally but the external effect is not published. Replay must publish exactly once with a unique receipt; a duplicate replay is refused.
2. **CRASH-B — publish happened, acknowledgement lost**: the effect is delivered but the outcome is unknown. The backend must NOT re-execute; it enters reconciliation (RECONCILED_SUCCEEDED / RECONCILED_FAILED) and is never blind-retried.
3. **CRASH-C — crash mid-DAG**: several effects are already published and receipted when the process dies. Resume completes the remaining tasks without re-executing earlier effects (exactly-once per effect key).
4. **CRASH-D — crash during the resume attempt**: the resume run itself dies. A second resume must not duplicate effects published before either crash (double-resume safety).

Adversarial probe requirement: a backend that resumes a task but duplicates an external effect must fail unless the outcome is reconciled AND the receipt is unique.

## Three load levels (identical for both backends)

- L1: 10 events/s (planning low point) — scheduling pass ~407 ms p95 (in-process, measured); durable: unavailable.
- L2: 34 events/s (planning point from S1-002) — scheduling pass ~1174 ms p95 (in-process, measured); durable: unavailable.
- L3: 100 events/s (burst) — scheduling pass ~3058 ms p95 (in-process, measured); durable: unavailable.

Every load level reports p95/p99 for the in-process backend and an explicit `unavailable` label for the durable backend (no production engine installed), plus a recovery-time observation (lease-expire -> recover_expired_runs -> resume_task) at each level; the durable side is explicitly unavailable.

## Replay semantics

Outbox/replay exactly-once, unknown-outcome -> reconciliation, unique receipts, fail-closed checkpoint verification — S1-004 safety semantics must remain intact; the replay-resume probe asserts them on every run.

## Bounded migration plan

Only a measured trigger (sustained p99 headroom exhausted, hard cross-host durability requirement, or audit/checkpoint store leaving SQLite) starts a bounded pilot; the pilot must preserve gateway-only effects and atomic transition+audit, and rollback if any S1-004 safety probe fails. No production backend is installed by this ticket.

## Expected outputs

bundle.json (this file), replay_resume_probe.py + comparability_probe.py (executable, verdict JSON + probe-results.json), README.md, and a research-plan evaluation that ends `pass` or `pass_with_limits`.

# S1-006 Feature Catalog — backend-scope dimensions

Maps the ticket scope (checkpoint/resume, crash/retry, idempotency, scheduling latency, operator visibility, test determinism, dependency-ready task execution) to implementation evidence (EP-11 and the QA2 decision).

| Scope item | In-process (current) | Durable-execution engine | Evidence refs |

| Checkpoint/resume | sha-verified, latest-consistent-only, immutable run lineage | event-history replay of activities (vendor semantics) | ENGINE-IMPL, TEMPORAL-DOCS |
| Crash/retry | lease expiry -> FAILED(crashed), bounded retries, resume | workflow replay after crash, activity retry policies | ENGINE-IMPL, TEMPORAL-WHITEPAPER |
| Idempotency | idempotency_key UNIQUE + UNKNOWN_OUTCOME -> reconciliation, unique receipts | activity IDs / event-store dedup, reconciliation still required at the effect boundary | GATEWAY-IMPL, TEMPORAL-WHITEPAPER |
| Scheduling latency | measured p95 407/1174/3058 ms (10/34/100 ev/s, scheduling pass); S1-002 p99 <= 7.4 ms end-to-end | unmeasured here; explicit unavailable label | S1-002-RAW, claim-bm-s1-006-latency |
| Operator visibility | single SQLite store + audit chain + wiki projection | separate service dashboard + event store (new ops surface) | JOURNAL-IMPL, TEMPORAL-DOCS |

mental_model.content:
# S1-006 Mental Model — how an operator reasons about the two backends

A Coordinator operating the MVP has one record of truth (SQLite/WAL + audit chain + wiki projection). The in-process scheduler fits that mental model: schedule a dependency-ready wave, watch readiness, inspect checkpoint rows and audit events in the same store, and resume from the latest consistent checkpoint after a crash. Leases bound ownership; idempotency keys make every retriable effect a keyed, reconciled unit; unknown outcomes surface as reconciliation-required items instead of silent retries.

A durable-execution engine changes the mental model: the event store is the source of truth for workflow progress, activities are replayed from history, and determinism constraints apply to workflow code (Azure Durable Functions literature: no non-deterministic calls, checkpoint-on-await; Temporal: event-history replay). Operators gain cross-host durability but lose the single-store audit/transition atomicity unless the gateway boundary is re-imposed on top of the engine. For the Coordinator the MVP mental model stays in-process; the durable model is documented and gated behind the migration trigger.

ontology.content:
# S1-006 Ontology — backend concepts

- **Backend**: the execution substrate that schedules and resumes tasks/runs (in_process_scheduler | durable_execution_engine).
- **Run**: an execution attempt of a Task with a lease, checkpoints, and a status life cycle; resumed runs reference resumed_from_run_id.
- **Checkpoint**: append-only record (seq, payload_path, sha256, work_completed/in_progress/next_action) enabling resume from the latest consistent state.
- **Outbox/replay**: the exactly-once delivery mechanism that replays the un-published subset of committed intents (never re-executes receipted effects).
- **Receipt**: unique identifier of one sink execution; uniqueness is the acceptance condition for any duplicate delivery.
- **Idempotency key**: sha256(key + op + canonical args) UNIQUE row recording first-seen run and outcome digest.
- **UNKNOWN_OUTCOME / reconciliation**: the only legal exit for delivered-but-unacknowledged effects; never blind retried.
- **Lease**: bounded ownership of a Run; expiry is the crash detector for recovery.
- **Event history (durable engines)**: append-only workflow event log replayed deterministically on resume (literature class).
- **Evidence requirements**: same-DAG comparison, 3 load levels, p95/p99, recovery observations or explicit unavailable labels.

mathematical_model.content:
# S1-006 Mathematical Model — latency, recovery, replay semantics

## Delivered-by definition

For every effect key k, let exec(k) = number of sink executions and rec(k) = number of unique receipts. Safety invariant (S1-004 SAF):

- Exactly-once: for crash-A/crash-C/crash-D replay, exec(k) = 1 and rec(k) = 1 for every effect executed by a completed run.
- Unknown-outcome path: exec(k) = 1, rec(k) = 1, activity ends RECONCILED_SUCCEEDED or RECONCILED_FAILED; never exec(k) > 1 without reconciliation.
- Duplicate delivery acceptance condition: exec(k) may exceed 1 ONLY IF reconciled(k) AND rec(k) == exec(k) (each delivery carries a unique receipt).

These are exactly the conditions the replay-resume probe enforces.

## Latency model

Scheduling-pass latency L(rate) for the in-process backend over the same chain DAG, measured: p95(10) ~= 407 ms, p95(34) ~= 1174 ms, p95(100) ~= 3058 ms; S1-002 end-to-end control-plane p99 <= 7.4 ms at 100 ev/s (cold). Durable-engine L is undefined in offline evidence: label = unavailable (no inference).

## Recovery model

R(rate) = time(lease-expire -> recover_expired_runs -> resume_task): ~438 / 558 / 583 ms for 10/34/100 ev/s. The durable engine's recovery time is labeled unavailable; the ticket does not claim parity.

## Comparability requirement

A latency comparison between two backends is admissible only if DAG(d) is identical across backends at every load level and every level includes a crash-recovery observation or explicit unavailable label; otherwise the comparison is incomparable (rejected).

synthesis_and_gaps.content:
# S1-006 Synthesis and Gaps

## Synthesis

Across architecture evidence (engine/gateway/journal/spec/invariants), formal lifecycle evidence (S1-004 SAF simulation), and benchmark evidence (S1-002 raw results + this ticket's scheduling-pass and recovery measurements), the in-process scheduler currently preserves the ticket's four criteria within the tested envelope:

1. **Durability**: task/run rows, checkpoints (sha-verified), lease-based crash detection, and atomic transition+audit in one SQLite/WAL store.
2. **Checkpoint/resume**: latest-consistent-only resume with immutable run lineage; corruption refuses resume.
3. **Deterministic testing**: deterministic fake worker and seeded simulation; no network/LLM dependency in the control plane.
4. **Latency**: S1-002 p99 <= 7.4 ms end-to-end; scheduling-pass p95 407/1174/3058 ms at 10/34/100 ev/s with recovery ~438/558/583 ms.

A durable-execution engine externalizes durability into an event store and re-performs scheduler duties, but in this offline environment its latency and recovery are unmeasured, its determinism obligations shift to developers, and it complicates the atomic transition+audit boundary unless re-encapsulated. QA2 therefore recommends the in-process scheduler, with a bounded migration plan triggered only by measured conditions.

## Gaps

- Durable-engine latency/recovery is unmeasured -> certified unavailable, not inferred (honest limitation).
- Scheduling-pass measurements are single-host, single-process observations; multi-process/container behavior is out of scope and unmeasured (mirrors S1-002 limitation).
- Literature verification is offline identity + content-scope review, not a live fetch or a vendor benchmark.
- The QA2 matrix scores (dimension/evidence) are structured design judgments grounded in cited evidence, not measured reliability claims.

independent_audit.content:
# S1-006 Independent Audit — pass with limits

Independent verifier review of the S1-006 producer bundle (subject producer: agentos-s1-006-producer).

## What was checked

- All repo-local source hashes recomputed from disk and matching declared values (including engine.py, gateway.py, journal.py, S1-004 simulation/bundle, S1-002 raw results, AGENTS.md, spec/SPEC.md, tickets doc).
- Claim-class coverage and mappings (architecture_fact/benchmark_measurement/tradeoff/failure_mode/decision) consistent with harness claim classes.
- QA2 decision matrix parses under agentos.s1-006-decision-matrix/v1: 8 scored dimensions, totals consistent (38 vs 21), 3 load levels with SAME dag_id across backends and p95/p99 + recovery or explicit unavailable labels, 6 failure scenarios complete.
- Adversarial comparability probes: different-DAG and recovery-omitting comparisons rejected as incomparable.
- Replay-resume probe: crash-A/B/C/D, naive-resume duplicate rejection, reconciled+unique-receipt acceptance, checkpoint-corruption fail-closed, dependency-ready ordering, S1-004 safety semantics intact.
- platform_plan sections present (Scope, Architecture, Workstreams, Milestones, Verification, Risks, Open decisions).

## Verdict

pass_with_limits. The decision (in-process scheduler) and bounded migration plan are justified by the cited evidence; the durable-engine cells are honestly unavailable.

platform_plan.content:
# Scope

S1-006 resolves QA2 for the Coordinator: the in-process scheduler remains the MVP execution backend, with an explicit backend boundary, a measured migration trigger, a rollback trigger, and evidence requirements for any future durable-execution change. Non-scope: no production vendor integration, no change to the current core runtime, no durability claim beyond tested local evidence, and no inferred durable-engine latency numbers.

# Architecture

The modular monolith stays (S1-005 QA1). Execution runs on the current engine: dependency-ready scheduling, run leases, sha-verified checkpoints, resume with immutable lineage, gateway idempotency/reconciliation, atomic transition+audit journal. The backend boundary is the Engine + ToolGateway + Journal contract: any future backend must keep effects gateway-only, consume approvals atomically exactly once, preserve unknown->reconciliation, and commit transition+audit atomically.

# Workstreams

1. Backend boundary: freeze Engine/ToolGateway/Journal contracts as the backend interface for the Coordinator (done in this ticket via claims + matrix).
2. Evidence harness: keep replay_resume_probe.py + comparability_probe.py as the regression gate for S1-004 safety semantics and same-DAG comparability.
3. Migration pilot (only on trigger): a bounded durable-engine pilot re-encapsulating the gateway/audit boundary behind the same probes; rollback if any probe fails.
4. Operator visibility: keep the wiki projection and audit anchor export as the single record-of-truth view.

# Milestones

- M1 (this ticket): QA2 decision recorded; matrix + probes evaluated pass/pass_with_limits; bundle persisted.
- M2: Coordinator consumption of the backend boundary (reference implementation unchanged, interface documented).
- M3 (conditional): bounded durable-engine pilot ONLY when a migration trigger fires; outcome = continue or rollback by probe evidence.
- M4: quarterly re-run of replay-resume + comparability probes against the running runtime to re-confirm safety semantics.

# Verification

Every bundle evaluation runs the executable probes: replay-resume (crash-A/B/C/D + near-miss duplicate + checkpoint corruption + dependency ordering + source-hash re-verification) and comparability (same-DAG, 3 load levels, p95/p99, recovery or unavailable labels, near-miss incomparable rejection, recommendation completeness, claim coverage, audit producer binding, live benchmark recorded). Final research-plan status must be pass or pass_with_limits; probes each run offline in < 60 s and the full probe budget is under 120 s.

# Risks

- Duplicate effects on resume: mitigated by the duplicate-effect guard (reconcile + unique receipt) and the replay probe.
- Unknown outcomes blind-retried: mitigated by gateway UNKNOWN_OUTCOME semantics and probe assertion.
- Incomparable latency comparisons: mitigated by the same-DAG + recovery-required comparability probe.
- Checkpoint corruption: mitigated by sha-verified fail-closed resume.
- Scope creep to a production backend: barred by non-scope claims and the audit's pass_with_limits framing.
- Single-host durability is host-disk-bound: documented as a limitation; cross-host durability triggers migration only via the measured trigger.

# Open decisions

1. Whether a future hard cross-host durability requirement should be met by a durable engine or by a sharded multi-SQLite arrangement: deferred until the trigger is real (evidence-before-pilot).
2. Whether the Coordinator should expose scheduling-pass p95 metrics to operators: recommended for the M4 monitoring gate, not decided here.
3. Whether the durable-engine pilot, if ever run, uses a self-hosted OSS engine or a vendor service: to be decided at pilot start with a fresh trust-boundary review (S1-003/S1-004 class evidence).

progress.content:
# S1-006 Progress

- 2026-08-31: bundle authored (sources/claims/artifacts/audit/probes), replay-resume + comparability probes written and verified offline on Windows (stdlib only).
- 2026-08-31: live scheduling-pass and recovery measurements recorded via comparability_probe.py --measure-only; values baked into the QA2 matrix and recorded in probe-results.json.
- Validation: research-plan evaluation to pass/pass_with_limits; any validator finding is fixed and re-run before closure.
- Outstanding: none (this ticket, Wave 2, Priority 1, owner architecture; dependencies S1-002 + S1-005 done).

limitations: Durable-execution-engine latency and recovery are unmeasured in this offline environment; their matrix cells are explicit unavailable labels, never inferred numbers.
Scheduling-pass and recovery observations are single-host, single-process measurements with live variance; they are observations recorded in probe-results.json, not production SLOs.
Literature sources (Temporal, Azure Durable Functions) were verified by offline identity and content-scope review; no live network fetch or vendor benchmark was performed.
Matrix dimension scores are structured design judgments grounded in the cited evidence, not measured reliability claims.
Producer and verifier are process-separated roles within one local environment, matching the S1-005 precedent; they are not independent human operators.
No production durable-execution backend was installed or exercised; the migration plan is bounded and door is left open to a future pilot under measured triggers.
